what: No Crop for Instagram fits your whole photo into a square 1:1, portrait 4:5, story 9:16 or landscape 16:9 frame, so nothing gets cut off when you post it. The empty space is filled with a blurred copy of the photo, a solid colour, a gradient or white.
Every result is 1080 pixels wide, the width Instagram and most other apps use. You can do one photo or a whole batch at once and download them together in a ZIP.
All processing happens in your browser; your photos are not uploaded. This tool is not connected to Instagram.
uses: Post a panorama or group photo in a square without cutting people off the sides.
Fit a portrait photo into a 9:16 story with a soft blurred background.
Place products on a clean white or brand-colour background with padding.
Share a phone screenshot as a neat 4:5 post with a gradient frame.
Give every photo in a carousel the same shape so none are cropped.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop photos here" or drop one or more photos on the box. Thumbnails appear underneath; tap one to preview it, or tap its × to remove it.
Under "Shape" pick Square 1:1, Portrait 4:5, Story 9:16 or Landscape 16:9.
In "Background" choose Blurred photo, Solid colour, Gradient or White. Use "Blur" to soften the blurred photo, or pick your colours.
Move "Padding" to leave a border around the photo, which looks good with white or colour backgrounds.
In "Download as" choose JPG for photos (smaller files) or PNG.
Click "Download". With several photos the button says "Download all … as ZIP" and you get one ZIP file with every image.
features: A soft blurred copy of your photo fills the space, as in popular apps.
Pick any colour or a two-colour gradient.
Add up to 30% space around the photo.
Process many photos at once and download them in one ZIP.
The whole photo is always visible.

example.title: Worked example: holiday photos for a carousel
example.text: Sam has five holiday photos, three landscape and two portrait. He drops all five, chooses Portrait 4:5 and Blurred photo, and sets "Padding" to 4%. He clicks "Download all 5 as ZIP" and gets no-crop-4x5.zip with five 1080 × 1350 JPGs, named like beach-4x5.jpg, ready to post as one carousel without anything cut off.

tips: Portrait 4:5 takes up the most space in the feed, so it is a good default for posts.
Use a higher blur for busy photos so the background does not distract from the picture.
A white background with 5–8% padding gives a clean, gallery-style look.
For a carousel, use the same shape and background for every photo so the set looks consistent.
Your settings are remembered on this device for next time; your photos are not.
problems: Only image files can be used. HEIC photos from iPhones must be exported as JPG first.
The background is not very blurred on my phone
Some older browsers do not support canvas blur, so a simpler blur method is used. Raise "Blur" for a softer look.
The photo looks small in the frame
Lower "Padding" to 0%. A very wide photo in a 9:16 frame will always leave a lot of background.
Some browsers block automatic downloads. Click the "Save …" button that appears next to "Download".
